text:
### Observed differences

- Participation changed for a group of activities: in the earlier window A25, A26, A27, A28, A31 and A36/A37/A42 each appeared in essentially all 200 cases; in the later window A25, A26, A28 and A31 still appear in all cases, while A27 appears in about 107 of 200 (~54 in 100) and A36, A37 and A42 in about 94–95 of 200 (~47 in 100). [POS003, POS006, POS007, POS008]

- A28 now directly follows A25: earlier, A25's outgoing transitions led to A42, A36 or A37 (about 34, 32 and 30 in 100 transitions) and A28 sat 4–5 positions after A25; in the later window about 97 in 100 of A25's outgoing transitions lead straight to A28, at a distance of one position in about 98 in 100 cases, and A28's mean position moved earlier (0.46 → 0.39 of the trace). [DIR001, LAG001, POS004]

- The A36/A37/A42 block moved from before A28/A26 to after A26: earlier, each block member preceded A26 and A28 in about 99–100 of 100 joint occurrences and sat at mean position ~0.40 of the trace; in the later window A26 precedes the block in nearly all of their ~47-in-100 co-occurrences, the block sits at mean position ~0.57, and A26's outgoing transitions now split between A27 (~52 in 100) and the block (~44 in 100). [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL014, REL015, REL016, POS006, POS007, POS008, DIR002]

- A27 and the block became alternatives: earlier they co-occurred in 100 of 100 cases (block first); in the later window they co-occur in about 1 in 100 cases or fewer, with A27 alone in ~53 in 100 cases and the block alone in ~46–47 in 100. [REL011, REL012, REL013]

- The rest of the segment is preserved: A26 still precedes A27 and A27 still precedes A31 where both occur, the block keeps its mixed internal order, still occurs as a trio and still precedes A31 when present, and the A26→A31 distance is two positions in ~53 in 100 later cases (A27 variant) versus four positions in ~43 in 100 (block variant), compared with two positions in ~98 in 100 earlier cases. [REL005, REL009, REL010, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, LAG005, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a specific restructuring hypothesis for the segment between A25 and A31, involving A25, A28, A26, A27, A31 and the block A36/A37/A42. In the earlier window every case ran A25 → the A36/A37/A42 block (in mixed order) → A28 → A26 → A27 → A31; in the later window A28 directly follows A25, and the block runs after A26 and before A31, where it has become an alternative to A27 — about 53 in 100 later cases contain A27 without the block and about 47 in 100 contain the block without A27, whereas all 200 earlier cases contained both. The order reversals between the block and A26/A28, the successor changes at A25 and A26, the collapse of A27–block co-occurrence from universal to near zero, and the A25→A28 lag dropping from 4–5 positions to 1 show this directly and consistently, and each difference exceeds about 199 of 200 random re-splits; with 44 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.5 expected if nothing had changed, sampling variation cannot explain the pattern as a whole. [DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, POS003, POS006, POS007, POS008]

Limitations: the relations are pairwise, so the evidence cannot show what triggers the choice between the A27 path and the block, nor fully rule out that the block overlaps the A26→A31 segment rather than running strictly between the two; a few lag items linking A25 with the block rest on only 1–2 later-window observations and were not used as support. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG006, LAG007, LAG009]

Other differences: minor position drifts — A25 sits slightly later (mean 0.34 → 0.37) and A31 slightly earlier (0.65 → 0.63) than before; A26 also sits earlier (0.60 → 0.54), consistent with the block no longer preceding it. [POS001, POS005, POS002]
